```{r update_fam}
mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam <-
  read.table(

    header = FALSE, sep = ""
  )

# colnames of $V1 to "id"

# colnames of $V6 to "population"
colnames(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam)[6] <- "population"

pop_table <- read.table("../data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_Borneo.poptable",
  sep = "\t", fill = TRUE
)
colnames(pop_table) <- c("IID", "V2", "FID", "Population", "V5", "V6", "V7")

# Remove the "RR"
mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$id <- sub("RR.*", "", mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$id)
mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$V2 <- sub("RR.*", "", mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$V2)
```

# Adjust for a second dataset with Merina labelled separately

```{r sep_merina, message = FALSE}
# back to character
mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population <-
  as.character(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population)

# Load fastmixture results
mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo <-
  gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_clean.gt")
qmats <-
  readRDS("~/Dropbox/gitdata/malagasy_diversity/data/intermediate/fastmixture/fastmixture_m.RData")
# tidy with the gt
mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo <- augment(get_q_matrix(qmats, k = 3, run = 1),
  data = mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo
)
# filter to merina
merina <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo %>% filter(population == "Merina")
# split groups
# .Q3 representing Asian ancestry and .Q2 representing African ancestry
merina$population <- ifelse(merina$.Q3 > 0.5, "MerinaA", "MerinaB")

merina$id <- sub("RR.*", "", merina$id)

# match V2 and merina$id and replace the population column in merina_fam with

  merina$population[matching_m], mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population

cat("Merina group > 0.5", length(which(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population == "MerinaA")))
cat("Merina group < 0.5", length(which(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population == "MerinaB")))
```

# Write .par files for ALDER

```{r write_par, message = FALSE}
# First, with Merina together
admix_list <- c(
  "Betsileo", "Betsimisaraka", "Diego", "Mikea",
  "Sakalava_Tsimihety", "Temoro", "Vezo", "Merina"
)

# List of reference-population sets
refpop_list <- list(
  c("Borneo", "Esan"),
  c("Sumba", "Esan"),
  c("Borneo", "Yoruba"),
  c("Sumba", "Yoruba"),
  c("Borneo", "Mozambique_Chopi"),
  c("Sumba", "Mozambique_Chopi")
)

# Fixed parameters
geno <- "../../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo.geno"
snp <- "../../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo.snp"
ind <- "../../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo.ind"

# Root output directory (do NOT modify inside the loop)
base_root <- "s07_ALDER_par_files"

write_par_files <- function(base_root,
                            admix_list,
                            refpop_list,
                            geno,
                            snp,
                            ind) {
  for (refset in refpop_list) {
    for (admix in admix_list) {
      folder <- paste(refset, collapse = "_")

      # Final output directory for this refpop set
      base_out <- file.path(getwd(), base_root, folder)

      if (!dir.exists(base_out)) {
        dir.create(base_out, recursive = TRUE)
      }

      # Filename for the .par file
      outfile <- sprintf(
        "%s/s07b_alder_%s.par",
        base_out, tolower(admix)
      )
      file.create(outfile)

      # Build the refpop string
      ref_str <- paste(refset, collapse = ";")

      # Write the .par file content
      par_text <- paste0(
        "genotypename: ", geno, "\n",
        "snpname: ", snp, "\n",
        "indivname: ", ind, "\n",
        "checkmap: YES\n",
        "jackknife: YES\n",
        "mindis: 0.005\n",
        "admixpop: ", admix, "\n",
        "refpops: ", ref_str, "\n",
        "raw_outname: ", file.path(
          base_out,
          paste0("alder_", tolower(admix), ".txt")
        ), "\n"
      )

      writeLines(par_text, con = outfile)
    }
  }
}

write_par_files(
  base_root,
  admix_list,
  refpop_list,
  geno,
  snp,
  ind
)

# And then for split Merina
geno <- "../../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.geno"
snp <- "../../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.snp"
ind <- "../../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.ind"

admix_list <- c("MerinaA", "MerinaB")

write_par_files(
  base_root,
  admix_list,
  refpop_list,
  geno,
  snp,
  ind
)
```


mindis: 0.005 - minimum genetic distance (in Morgans) at which to start
curve fitting (default: determined using LD correlation).
<https://comppopgenworkshop2019.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contents/06_alder/alder.html>
States that the default calculates the correlation in LD decay between
the target and each reference, and uses 'the minimum distance that shows
no correlation in both references.' 'If it continues beyond 2 cM (due to
either a strong bottleneck or admixture in a reference), the program
aborts.' In example with Merina as Target and Esan and Borneo as
reference, setting mindis to default causes the program to abort.

@TODO What does mindis do to the results?

If mindis is automatically chosen, Betsileo and Merina/Merina A runs fail with:

'too much long-range LD; not plotting LD curve'
'fit start = inf because of long-range LD correlation; exiting'

This is likely due to strong bottleneck in Asian ancestry component, given that
it fails only for populations with a larger Asian ancestry component. If it was 
due to admixture in the reference, we might expect it to fail for all target populations.

checkmap: YES
binsize: 0.0005 default - genetic distance resolution (in
Morgans) - the size of bins that ALDER splits the genome up into, used
to calculate the distance between the bins of two snps as opposed to the
distance between the each individual pair of snps, for computational
efficiency
jackknife: YES - outputs results from leave-one-chromosome-out jackknifing

# Run bash scripts in a loop

```{bash run_alder, echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
CODE_ROOT=~/Git/malagasy_diversity/code/s07_ALDER_par_files
RESULT_ROOT=~/Git/malagasy_diversity/results/s07_ALDER

for FOLDER in "$CODE_ROOT"/*/; do
    
    # Strip path and trailing slash → e.g., Borneo_Esan
    BASENAME=$(basename "$FOLDER")

    echo "Processing reference set: $BASENAME"

    # Make matching output directory
    OUTDIR="$RESULT_ROOT/$BASENAME"
    mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"

    # Enter the folder containing the .par files
    cd "$FOLDER" || continue

    # Loop through each .par file
    for PAR in *.par; do
        LOG="$OUTDIR/${PAR%.par}.log"

        echo "  Running ALDER on $PAR"
        alder -p "$PAR" > "$LOG" 2>&1
    done

    echo "Finished $BASENAME"
    echo "----------------------"
done

```

# Get and process outputs

```{r process_outputs, message = FALSE}
res_folders <- list.dirs("../results/s07_ALDER",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = FALSE
)

get_logs <- function(res_folders) {
  files <- c()
  for (folder in res_folders) {
    new_logs <- list.files(folder,
      pattern = ".log",
      full.names = TRUE
    )
    files <- c(files, new_logs)
  }
  return(files)
}

files <- get_logs(res_folders)



# remove any from files that don't have 'alder' in  the name
files <- files[grepl("_alder", files)]

# use readLines to read each of files
logs <- lapply(files, readLines)

# Extract "DATA:" lines from each log file in the list
data_lines <- lapply(
  logs,
  function(log_file) {
    log_file[grepl("^DATA:",
      log_file,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )]
  }
)


# Extract the first line from each element in data_lines
first_lines <- sapply(data_lines, function(x) if (length(x) > 0) x[1] else NA)

# Split each first "DATA:" line by backslash "\\"
split_data <- lapply(first_lines, function(x) strsplit(x, "\t")[[1]])

result <- do.call(rbind, split_data)
result <- as.data.frame(result, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# remove NA row
result <- result[complete.cases(result), ]




# Extract the second line from each element in data_lines
second_lines <- sapply(data_lines, function(x) if (length(x) > 0) x[2] else NA)

# split second lines by "\"
split_data2 <- lapply(second_lines, function(x) strsplit(x, "\t")[[1]])
# apply colnames
colnames(result) <- split_data2[[2]]
# remove first two columns
result <- result[, -c(1, 2)]

# split $`2-ref decay` into 2 columns
split_dates <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(result$`2-ref decay`, " "))
# remove the middle column
split_dates <- split_dates[, -2]
# add column names
colnames(split_dates) <- c("admixture_date", "CI")
# turn into a dataframe
split_dates <- as.data.frame(split_dates)
# make numeric
split_dates$admixture_date <- as.numeric(split_dates$admixture_date)
split_dates$CI <- as.numeric(split_dates$CI)
result <- cbind(result, split_dates)

# split $`2-ref amp_exp` into 2 columns
split_amp <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(result$`2-ref amp_exp`, " "))
# remove the middle column
split_amp <- split_amp[, -2]
# add column names
colnames(split_amp) <- c("amp_exp", "amp_exp_CI")
# turn into a dataframe
split_amp <- as.data.frame(split_amp)
# make numeric
split_amp$amp_exp <- as.numeric(split_amp$amp_exp)
split_amp$amp_exp_CI <- as.numeric(split_amp$amp_exp_CI)
result <- cbind(result, split_amp)


# Process each log file
amp_aff_lines <- lapply(logs, function(log_text) {
  # Find the index of the header
  header_index <- grep("Computing 2-ref weighted LD with weights...", log_text)

  if (length(header_index) == 0) {
    return(NA) # Return NA if the header is not found
  }

  # Search for 'amp_aff:' after the header
  amp_aff_index <- grep(
    "amp_aff:",
    log_text[(header_index + 1):length(log_text)]
  )

  if (length(amp_aff_index) == 0) {
    return(NA) # Return NA if no 'amp_aff:' line is found
  }

  # Extract the first matching line
  log_text[header_index + amp_aff_index[1]]
})

amp_aff_lines <- do.call(rbind, amp_aff_lines)
amp_aff_lines <- amp_aff_lines[complete.cases(amp_aff_lines), ]
amp_aff_lines <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(amp_aff_lines, " "))
result$amp_aff <- as.numeric(amp_aff_lines[, 8])

result$`test pop` <- factor(result$`test pop`,
  levels = c(
    "Betsimisaraka", "Temoro", "MerinaB",
    "Betsileo", "Mikea", "Merina",
    "Sakalava_Tsimihety", "Vezo", "MerinaA",
    "Diego"
  )
)

# save result
saveRDS(result, "../results/s07_ALDER/alder_results_all.RData")
```

'Also note that we do not use the jackknife to
   estimate bias: i.e., for any inference of the form "x +/- y", x is
   computed using data from all chromosomes and y is the standard
   error obtained from the jackknife.' README file for ALDER

# Example LD curve plots

'Weighted LD curves computed on real populations often exhibit a nonzero
horizontal asymptote contrary to the exact exponential decay formulas we
have derived above. Such behavior can be caused by assortative mating
resulting in subpopulations structured by ancestry percentage in
violation of our model. We show in Appendix A that if we instead model
the admixed population as consisting of randomly mating subpopulations
with heterogeneous amounts α—now a random variable—of mixed ancestry,
our equations for the curves take the form' (Loh et al 2013)

$$
E[\alpha(d)] = M e^{-nd} + K
$$

'We fit discretized weighted LD curves as from Equation 9, using
least-squares to find best-fit parameters.' (Loh et al 2013)

The following plotting code is adapted from
<https://comppopgenworkshop2019.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contents/06_alder/alder.html>
Which describes as: E[Y] = M times e \ ^-nd + K

Adjusting the parameters refA and refB will print all LD curves for this combination.

```{r plot_curves}
result <- readRDS("../results/s07_ALDER/alder_results_all.RData")

res_folders <- list.dirs("../code/s07_ALDER_par_files",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = FALSE
)

get_txt <- function(res_folders) {
  files <- c()
  for (folder in res_folders) {
    new_logs <- list.files(folder,
      pattern = ".txt",
      full.names = TRUE
    )
    files <- c(files, new_logs)
  }
  return(files)
}

files <- get_txt(res_folders)

# remove jackknifing per-chromosome .txt files
files <- files[!grepl(".txt-", files)]

plot_curves <- function(refA, refB, files, result) {
  result_sub <- subset(
    result,
    result$`ref A` == refA & result$`ref B` == refB
  )

  ref_combo <- paste0(refA, "_", refB)
  files <- files[grepl(ref_combo, files)]

  counter <- 1
  plot_list <- list()

  for (i in files) {
    d1 <- read.table(i, header = FALSE)

    n <- result_sub[counter, ]$admixture_date ## decay - estimated admixture date
    M <- result_sub[counter, ]$amp_exp ## amp_exp -
    K <- result_sub[counter, ]$amp_aff ## amp_aff -

    d1 <- d1[-nrow(d1), ]

    colnames(d1) <- c("Dist", "weightedLD", "npairs")
    xv <- as.vector(d1$Dist) ## distance between SNP bins (cM) - genetic distance

    prdv <- M * exp(-1 * n * xv / 100) + K # E[Y] = M times e^-nd + K

    this_plot <- ggplot(d1, aes(x = Dist, y = weightedLD)) +
      geom_point(color = "blue", shape = 4) +
      geom_line(aes(y = prdv), color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
      labs(
        x = "Genetic distance (cM)",
        y = "Weighted LD",
        title = paste("Weighted LD decay curve for", result_sub[counter, ]$`test pop`)
      ) +
      theme_minimal()

    plot_list[[counter]] <- this_plot
    counter <- counter + 1
  }
  return(plot_list)
}

# Run the function
refA <- "Borneo"
refB <- "Mozambique_Chopi"
res <- plot_curves(refA, refB, files, result)

for (p in res) print(p)
```

## Recording R environment

Part of ensuring our workflow is reproducible is to keep track of the R
environment. We will automatically save our R environment into a file
called `r_environment.json`.

```{r save-r-environment, echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
filename_rmd <- "s07_ALDER.Rmd"
filename_renv <- paste0(
  res_dir, "/renv_",
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(filename_rmd)),
  ".json"
)
renv::lockfile_write(renv::lockfile_create(), file = filename_renv)

```
